Forget passive income — sentence by sentence

A business creator's 73-second case against early passive income — cut into 19 loopable thought units (2-5.5 s each) so every clip fits in your ear. Blue = her voice (semitones vs her 169 Hz median; shaded area = loudness). ▶ play · ⟳ loop · 0.75× slow · ● record yourself — your contour is drawn dashed on top. '…' marks a thought that continues in the next clip.

Overview — pick a chapter

Semitones are relative to the speaker's overall median (0 line), the same reference for every clip. Your recorded contour is plotted against your own median, so only the shape is compared. Floor line = this clip's 5th percentile; ceiling guide = +4 st.
The sentence text itself is drawn as a melody — each word colored (blue = low, red = high) and raised or lowered by its pitch vs the speaker's median, while word SIZE shows loudness — so a big gray word is loud-but-flat, and a small red word is a pitch peak without volume. The ▲/🔊/⏱ note under each sentence names the highest, loudest, and longest word: when the amber flag says pitch peak ≠ loudness peak, that sentence is direct evidence that English prominence is carried by the pitch move, not by volume or length. After you record, a second "you" line renders your melody and loudness on the same words (relative to your own median and your own loudest word, so only the shape is compared). Longer sentences show a thought groups row — pick a group and play / loop / record work on just that span (the shaded region); "all" returns to the full sentence. Recordings become takes under each card — record as many as you like and click a chip to switch between them. ★ keeps a take in this browser (on this device) across reloads; ☁ publishes it onto this site so anyone opening the page — e.g. your coach — can hear it (public; one-time token setup); ⬇ downloads it as an audio file; unstarred takes vanish when you leave the page. Dashed chips are published takes.
